findings.claim: `DESKTOP_MIN` and `DESKTOP_QUERY` are new exports that nothing imports. Only `layout.ts` uses them, so they are dead public surface that the next night may take for a shared API.
findings.evidence: In `layout.ts`: `export const DESKTOP_MIN = {` (line 9) and `export const DESKTOP_QUERY = ...` (line 17). Grep for `DESKTOP_MIN|DESKTOP_QUERY` over /work (excluding node_modules) matches only src/ui/layout.ts:9, 17 and 21. No file in src/ or tests/ imports them. inventory.md lists both as exports. `COARSE_POINTER` and `watchDesktop` are the only exports that are imported (by touch-controls.ts, hud.ts and keycap-legend.ts).
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the `export` keyword from `DESKTOP_MIN` and `DESKTOP_QUERY` in src/ui/layout.ts so they become module-private constants.

findings.claim: The new `.ui-keycap` rule in the same file re-declares what `.ui-panel` and `.ui-panel--cream` already provide (ink outline, radius, HUD shadow, cream background with ink text). The legend could compose those existing classes the way every other HUD widget does.
findings.evidence: `.ui-keycap` (components.css:243-247): `border: var(--outline-default) solid var(--color-ink); border-radius: var(--radius-rect); box-shadow: var(--shadow-hud); background: var(--color-cream); color: var(--color-ink);`. This repeats `.ui-panel` (lines 72-76: `border: var(--outline-default) solid var(--color-ink); border-radius: var(--radius-rect); box-shadow: var(--shadow-hud);`) and `.ui-panel--cream` (lines 88-91: `background: var(--color-cream); color: var(--color-ink);`) declaration for declaration. hud.ts already composes `'ui-panel ui-panel--mustard ui-hud-best'` the same way.
findings.suggestedFix: In keycap-legend.ts `key()`, use the class `ui-panel ui-panel--cream ui-keycap` and delete the five duplicated declarations (border, border-radius, box-shadow, background, color) from `.ui-keycap`. Keep `.ui-keycap--primary` for the rally-red key.

findings.claim: The keycaps only ever show on desktop, but they get the phone's 3px outline. UI_RULES §3 asks for 4px outlines on desktop, and so does the spec ('4 px ink outlines'). Every other desktop HUD outline in this diff uses --desktop-outline: the HUD panels, PAUSE and the legend panel itself. The keycaps are the one exception.
findings.evidence: components.css adds `.ui-keycap { … border: var(--outline-default) solid var(--color-ink); … }`. In tokens.css, --outline-default is 3px and --desktop-outline is 4px. keycap-legend.ts only makes the legend visible when `desktop && firstLap`, so a keycap never renders outside desktop mode. The keycap is calc(var(--space-s6) + var(--space-s1)) = 36px tall, so the 2px under-32px tier doesn't apply either. UI_RULES §3: 'Outline: solid ink. 2px if the element is under 32px, 3px default, 4px if over 120px or on desktop.' In screenshot 1440x900/stage/hud--first-lap.png the keycap outlines are visibly thinner than the 4px outline on the legend panel around them. Reproduce: render stage hud--first-lap at 1440×900 without touch. getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.ui-keycap')).borderTopWidth returns '3px'; it should be '4px'.
findings.suggestedFix: In `.ui-keycap`, use `border: var(--desktop-outline) solid var(--color-ink);`, or add `.ui-keys .ui-keycap { border-width: var(--desktop-outline); }` in keycap-legend.css to match how hud.css handles desktop outlines.

findings.claim: The spec summary says the minimap and PAUSE are drawn at ×1.45 on desktop, but no test measures either size. Deleting the desktop size rules for both leaves every new test passing.
findings.evidence: Mutation: delete `.ui-hud.is-desktop .ui-hud-map { width: calc(... * var(--desktop-scale)); height: ... }` (src/ui/hud.css:83-86), or delete the `.ui-hud.is-desktop .ui-hud-pause { width/min-height ... }` rule (hud.css:90-93). AC1 checks only posSize, lapSize, labelSizes, the outlines of .ui-hud-pos/.ui-hud-lap/.ui-hud-time, pos.left/top and `DESKTOP.width - d.pause.right`. PAUSE's right edge stays 32px whatever its width, and the minimap box is never read. So both mutations survive, and the HUD would show a phone-sized minimap and PAUSE at 1440×900.
findings.suggestedFix: In the AC1 test's snapshot(), also record box(q('.ui-hud-map')) and box(q('.ui-hud-pause')). Assert that their desktop width and height are 1.45× the phone context's values, within ±1px.

findings.claim: AC4 only checks that each of the four arrow keycaps contains some `<svg>`. It doesn't check which arrow is on which key, or that GAS uses the rally-red primary keycap from the spec. Arrows that are swapped or pointing the wrong way, or a cream GAS key, all pass.
findings.evidence: Mutations in src/ui/keycap-legend.ts:217-219 that survive: (a) `item([key(icon('key-right')), key(icon('key-left'))], 'STEER')`, which swaps the steer arrows; (b) `item([key(icon('key-up'))], 'BRAKE')`, which puts the up arrow on BRAKE; (c) `item([key(icon('key-up'), true)], 'GAS')` → `item([key(icon('key-up'))], 'GAS')`, which drops ui-keycap--primary, so the key isn't rally-red as the spec summary requires. The test's only icon assertion is `for (const k of iconKeys) expect(k.querySelector('svg')).not.toBeNull();`.
findings.suggestedFix: In AC4, compare each keycap's SVG polygon `points` with the matching entry from a fresh icon('key-left'|'key-right'|'key-up'|'key-down') in the order left, right, up, down. Also assert that the GAS keycap has the class ui-keycap--primary and the others don't.

findings.claim: The spec says the mode updates live on resize, but no test checks that the keycap legend follows a resize. The happy-dom matchMedia stub never fires 'change', and the browser AC6 test opens a fresh page per viewport. The legend can ignore resize changes and every test still passes.
findings.evidence: Mutation in src/ui/keycap-legend.ts:232-235: replace `watchDesktop((d) => { desktop = d; update(); });` with `desktop = matchMedia(DESKTOP_QUERY).matches; update();`. AC3-AC6 in keycap-legend.test.ts build the UI after useDevice() and never change the device. desktop-hud.test.ts AC6 uses a new context per viewport, and AC2 (the only resize test) reads `.ui-hud-pos__n` and never the legend. The mutation survives: during lap 1, a desktop window resized below 1224×566 keeps showing the legend over a phone-sized HUD.
findings.suggestedFix: In desktop-hud.test.ts AC2 (or a new test), render 'hud--first-lap' at 1440×900. Call page.setViewportSize({width:1000,height:700}) and poll until the legend is not visible, then resize back and poll until it is visible again.

rulings.trace: grep DESKTOP_MIN|DESKTOP_QUERY: only src/ui/layout.ts:9,17,21. They are unused outside the module, but they are correct, documented and derived from tokens.
rulings.reason: Exporting two well-named, documented constants that are not imported elsewhere is harmless and a style preference. Nothing behaves wrongly, and the spec asked for the threshold to be computed in one place, which is what layout.ts does.

rulings.trace: src/ui/components.css .ui-keycap declares `border: var(--outline-default) solid var(--color-ink); border-radius: var(--radius-rect); box-shadow: var(--shadow-hud); background: var(--color-cream); color: var(--color-ink);`. .ui-panel (components.css:72-76) declares the same border, border-radius and box-shadow, and .ui-panel--cream (88-91) the same background and color, declaration for declaration. hud.ts already composes panel classes ('ui-panel ui-panel--mustard ui-hud-best'). .ui-keycap--primary is declared later in the file with equal specificity, so it would still override the cream background. Composing 'ui-panel ui-panel--cream ui-keycap' in keycap-legend.ts key() gives the same computed style.
rulings.reason: The five declarations duplicate the existing .ui-panel and .ui-panel--cream classes exactly, and composing those classes is the established pattern. The fix is safe because the primary modifier comes later in the cascade and still wins.

rulings.trace: Ran `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/verify/R4-1.test.ts`. The test builds the harness screens, renders stage hud--first-lap at 1440x900 without touch, and reads getComputedStyle(.ui-keycap).borderTopWidth for all 5 keycaps. It failed with `expected Set{'3px'} to deeply equal Set{'4px'}`. The cause is that .ui-keycap uses var(--outline-default)=3px, and only .ui-keys__panel gets --desktop-outline.
rulings.reason: UI_RULES §3 says outlines are 4px on desktop, and §5 and the spec ask for 4px outlines on desktop. Keycaps render only in desktop mode and are 36px tall, so neither the 2px nor the 3px tier applies. They measure 3px.

rulings.trace: tests/ui/desktop-hud.test.ts snapshot() (lines 35-61) records posSize, lapSize, labelSizes, outlines, pos box, pause box, touchVisible and legendVisible. It never reads .ui-hud-map. The only assertion on pause is `DESKTOP.width - d.pause.right === 32` (line 95), and that holds whatever PAUSE's width, because .ui-hud__tr is right-anchored at --desktop-margin (hud.css:139-142). Deleting hud.css:170-173 (map ×--desktop-scale) or 177-180 (pause ×--desktop-scale) therefore leaves AC1, AC2 and AC6 passing. No other test file covers these rules. The spec summary requires 'the minimap and PAUSE button at ×1.45'.
rulings.reason: The spec's summary feature (minimap and PAUSE at ×1.45) is implemented in hud.css:170-180, but no test measures it, so a regression would go unnoticed. A new test comparing desktop and phone boxes would pass on the current code.

rulings.trace: src/ui/keycap-legend.ts:25-28 builds the items key-left/key-right STEER, key-up primary GAS, key-down BRAKE, and ESC PAUSE. tests/ui/keycap-legend.test.ts AC4 checks only `k.querySelector('svg')` for each of the 4 icon keys, plus the ESC text. AC3 checks labels and AC5/AC6 check visibility. icons.ts:14-17 defines distinct polygons for key-left, key-right, key-up and key-down, but no test compares them. No test checks ui-keycap--primary either. Swapping the icons or dropping the `true` primary flag leaves every test passing. The spec summary requires '↑ on rally-red, as in the mockup'.
rulings.reason: The right arrow-to-key mapping and the rally-red GAS key are spec requirements that no test pins down, so swapped arrows (a user-visible bug) would pass. The current code is correct, so a new test asserting them would pass.

rulings.trace: keycap-legend.ts:40-43 updates `desktop` through watchDesktop's 'change' listener (layout.ts:20-24). In keycap-legend.test.ts, useDevice() stubs matchMedia with an EventTarget that never dispatches 'change', and every test builds the UI after fixing the device. In desktop-hud.test.ts, AC6 opens a fresh context per viewport, and AC2 (the only resize test, lines 106-118) reads only .ui-hud-pos__n and outlines, never the legend. Replacing the watchDesktop call with a one-off matchMedia(...).matches read would therefore pass every test. The spec summary says 'the mode updates live on resize'.
rulings.reason: No test checks that the legend's live response to a resize works, even though the spec requires live mode updates. A browser test that resizes the first-lap stage would pass on the current code and catch the regression.

fixes.summary: Removed the duplicated keycap styling by reusing the existing panel classes. In src/ui/keycap-legend.ts, key() now gives each keycap the classes 'ui-panel ui-panel--cream ui-keycap', the same way hud.ts builds 'ui-panel ui-panel--mustard ui-hud-best'. In src/ui/components.css, I deleted the five declarations from .ui-keycap that .ui-panel and .ui-panel--cream already set (border, border-radius, box-shadow, background, color) and updated its comment. .ui-keycap--primary has the same specificity and comes later in the file, so the GAS key is still rally-red with a cream glyph. The legend sits outside .ui-hud, so the desktop rule `.ui-hud.is-desktop .ui-panel` (4px outline) doesn't reach the keycaps, and their computed style is unchanged. This is a duplication finding, so behaviour is meant to stay the same. The new guard test therefore passes both before and after the change. I checked that it does catch a regression: with the panel classes taken off the keycaps (the CSS already reduced), it fails. It renders the hud--first-lap stage at 1440×900 in Chromium and checks that the four cream keycaps compute the same border, radius, shadow, background and colour as the token variables (--outline-default, --color-ink, --radius-rect, --shadow-hud, --color-cream), and that GAS computes the rally-red/cream pair. pnpm typecheck passes and pnpm test passes (82 files, 612 tests). The 1440×900 first-lap screenshot shows the legend looking as it did before.

The finding is real. In the hud--first-lap stage at 1440×900, every keycap renders with a 3px border. I confirmed this with a new red test, then added `.ui-keys .ui-keycap { border-width: var(--desktop-outline); }` to keycap-legend.css, and the new test went green. But an existing test, tests/ui/keycap-style.test.ts (from an earlier finding, R3-2), checks that keycaps on that same 1440×900 desktop stage use exactly `var(--outline-default)`, which is 3px. With the fix in place that test fails (612 passed, 1 failed). Tests are append-only, so I'm not allowed to change it. That means the fix can't pass the gates, and the two requirements can't both hold under the rules. I reverted everything: the CSS change and my new test file. The tree is back as it was, and pnpm test passes all 82 files. The owner needs to decide which is right: UI_RULES §3 (4px on desktop) or the R3-2 test (3px). If §3 wins, that test needs to be retired before this fix can land.

This was a gap in test coverage, so I added a test and left the code alone. The new file tests/ui/desktop-hud-scale.test.ts (named AC1) uses the same Chromium harness as desktop-hud.test.ts. It renders the hud--mid-race stage twice, once at 1440×900 without touch and once at 844×390 with touch. In each it measures the bounding boxes of .ui-hud-map and .ui-hud-pause. It then checks that each box's desktop width and height equal the phone value × tokens.desktop.scale (imported from @tokens), within ±1px, and that the phone boxes aren't empty. The test passes on the current code. I tried both mutations the reviewer named and it fails on each: without the desktop PAUSE size rule it is off by 21.6px, and without the desktop minimap size rule by 46.8px. I restored hud.css byte-for-byte afterwards. I didn't touch any src/ file or existing test. pnpm typecheck passes, and pnpm test passes (83 files, 613 tests). I couldn't run eslint because it isn't installed in this environment.

The finding is about a weak test. The legend code is already correct, so nothing in src/ changed. I added one new test file, tests/ui/keycap-legend-keys.test.ts. It sets up a desktop matchMedia (fine pointer, 1440×900), resets and syncs the race UI on lap 1, finds the "Keyboard controls" group, and groups its keycaps by label. For STEER, GAS and BRAKE it compares each keycap's SVG polygon `points` with those of a fresh icon('key-left'/'key-right'), icon('key-up') and icon('key-down'), in that order. It also checks that only the GAS keycap has `ui-keycap--primary`, the class that gives it the rally-red background in components.css; the steer, brake and ESC keycaps don't. Red/green: I applied each of the reviewer's three mutations to src/ui/keycap-legend.ts in turn: steer arrows swapped, the up arrow on BRAKE, and the primary flag removed from GAS. The new test failed every time. After restoring the file (checked byte-for-byte with cmp) it passes. pnpm typecheck is clean and pnpm test passes: 84 files, 614 tests.

This finding was about test strength: nothing checked that the keycap legend responds to a resize. The game code already handles it correctly, so I left src/ unchanged and only added a new browser test, tests/ui/keycap-legend-resize.test.ts. The test builds the screens harness and renders the 'hud--first-lap' stage in Chromium at 1440×900 with no touch. It checks that the "Keyboard controls" group is visible. It then resizes the page to 1000×700 and polls until the group is hidden, resizes back to 1440×900 and polls until it is visible again, then shrinks the page once more and checks the group hides. Finally it opens a fresh page at 1000×700, checks the legend is hidden, grows the page to 1440×900 and polls until the legend appears. Red/green: I temporarily applied the reviewer's mutation, replacing the watchDesktop call in src/ui/keycap-legend.ts with a one-off matchMedia(DESKTOP_QUERY).matches read. The new test failed: the legend stayed visible after the resize to 1000×700. I then restored the original file and confirmed it is byte-identical; the test passes against the current code. pnpm typecheck is clean and pnpm test passes (85 files, 615 tests).
